lessons.title: Turning Pictures into Numbers
lessons.content_md:
# Turning Pictures into Numbers 👁️

When you look at a photo of a cat, your eyes see fur, ears, and whiskers.

When a computer looks at that exact same photo, it sees nothing but a massive spreadsheet of numbers.

## The Pixel Grid 🔢

Every digital image is made of tiny dots called **pixels**. 

If you zoom all the way into a black-and-white photo, you'll see a grid. Each square in that grid is assigned a number from 0 (pure black) to 255 (pure white). 

So, an image of a cat isn't a "picture" to a computer; it's just a matrix of numbers like this:

```
[0,   50,  120]
[255, 200, 10]
[10,  0,   255]
```

## Finding Edges

How does the AI know it's looking at a cat? It uses math to find **Edges**.

If the AI is scanning the numbers and sees a bunch of 0s (black) suddenly turn into a bunch of 255s (white), it mathematically calculates that there must be a sharp edge right there. 

By finding thousands of these edges, the hidden layers of the neural network piece together shapes, textures, and eventually, a cat!

<flipcard front="👁️ How does a computer see an image?" back="Computers see images as massive grids of numbers, representing the color value of each pixel."></flipcard>
